name: jsonencode
summary: Encodes MATLAB values as JSON text.
doc:
- A scalar becomes a JSON number, boolean or string; a vector a flat array; a matrix or N-d array nested arrays, its first dimension outermost (`eye(2)` is `[[1,0],[0,1]]`).
- A character vector becomes a string; a character matrix an array of its rows; a string array strings, nested as a numeric array is.
- A cell array becomes a flat array of its elements in column-major order.
- A struct becomes an object; a struct array an array of objects, nested as a numeric array is.
- An integer is written as an integer; any other number as the shortest text that reads back as the same double.

Options:
- `ConvertInfAndNaN` (true): Inf and NaN become `null`; false writes `Infinity`, `-Infinity` and `NaN`.
- `PrettyPrint` (false): true indents by two spaces, one value per line.

Complex numbers and sparse arrays are refused, as MATLAB refuses them.
differs: Without MATLAB's own documentation of the number format, numbers are written as Octave 11.1 writes them: 1.5e-7, 0.1, 123456789012.
MATLAB's tables, datetime, categorical, containers.Map, enumerations and object arrays are not encoded: Sagebrush lacks those types, or (object arrays) refuses them.

name: jsondecode
summary: Parses JSON text into MATLAB values.
doc:
- `null` becomes `[]`, and NaN inside an array of numbers.
- A number becomes a double, a boolean a logical, a string a character vector.
- An object becomes a struct, its names made valid as `matlab.lang.makeValidName` makes them.
- An array of numbers (and nulls) becomes a column vector; an array of booleans a logical one; an array of numeric (or of logical) arrays of one size an array of one more dimension, the first; other nested arrays stay cell arrays.
- An array of objects with the same names in the same order becomes a struct array; any other array a cell array.

The text is refused when it is over 67,108,864 characters or nested more than 512 levels deep.

examples.expected:
v = 

  struct with fields:

    a: [3×1 double]
    b: [1×1 struct]
    d: {2×1 cell}

differs: Objects whose names are the same but in another order give a cell array of structs, as Octave 11.1 gives (MATLAB's documentation says only "same field names").
